lesson.title: kein vs nicht Choice Gym
lesson.subtitle: Twenty prompts: noun phrases take kein, verbs take nicht

hook.title: The Choice Machine
hook.content: Every German negation is a fork: is the sentence killing a THING or an ACTION? Kill the thing — kein: Ich habe kein Haus, keine Zeit, keinen Kaffee. Kill the action — nicht: Ich kann nicht kommen, das ist nicht gut. English uses one not for both; German forces you to name the victim. Twenty prompts today, each a fork. Choose wrong and the explanation shows you what kind of thing you were trying to kill.

footnotes.title: The Arithmetic of kein
footnotes.content: kein is 'not one': ni + ein, exactly like English none. So it never appears with actions — you cannot 'not-one' a verb. If there is an ein (or a bare plural noun) in the sentence you are negating, the answer is some form of kein.

pattern.title: The Fork, Then the Form
pattern.content: Step one — the fork: negating a noun phrase? kein. Negating a verb, adjective, or adverb? nicht. Step two — the form: kein declines exactly like ein (kein Haus, keine Zeit, keinen Kaffee — Him-Case included). Step three — the place: nicht usually lands right where the action dies, at the end of a simple clause (Ich weiß es nicht), or directly before the word it targets (Das ist nicht gut, nicht heute — 'not today').
pattern.linguist_note: Full-sentence denials take nicht: 'Nein' negates the whole world of a yes/no answer, nicht negates the verb inside the sentence, and kein negates a noun. Three tools, three targets — English merged them all into one not.

exercises.prompt: 'Ich trinke _____ Kaffee.' (I am not drinking coffee — kill the coffee)
exercises.meaning: Ich trinke keinen Kaffee = I am not drinking coffee
exercises.explanation: Noun phrase → kein, and der Kaffee is a masculine object: the Him-Case makes it keinen.

exercises.prompt: 'Ich kann _____ kommen.' (I cannot come — kill the coming)
exercises.meaning: Ich kann nicht kommen = I cannot come
exercises.explanation: Verbs take nicht — you cannot 'not-one' an action.

exercises.meaning: Wir haben keine Zeit = We have no time
exercises.explanation: die Zeit is feminine: kein takes -e, exactly like ein → eine.

exercises.prompt: Complete the ein → kein Negation matrix for the masculine accusative ('no / not a'):
exercises.explanation: kein is simply k- + ein: wherever ein becomes einen, kein becomes keinen (Ich bekomme keinen Kaffee, ich weiß es). [Ref: Ich habe kein Haus, Ich weiß es nicht, Das ist nicht gut, Ich bekomme keinen Kaffee]

exercises.prompt: Say in German: "I have no time / I do not have time"
exercises.meaning: I have no time / I do not have time
exercises.explanation: English negates the verb ('do not have'); German negates the noun ('no time') — keine Zeit, the honest fork.
exercises.idea: I have no time / I do not have time
idea_parts: I do not have time (verb in position 2)
cues: Start with "Ich" and anchor "habe" in position 2.

summary.outcome: Choose kein vs nicht instantly and decline kein through all three genders.
summary.takeaway: Noun phrases take kein ('not one'), verbs and adjectives take nicht ('no-thing') — name the victim, then pick the weapon.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Next: the nicht position map — where exactly the no-thing lands in the sentence.

twist.prompt: Without looking back — rebuild the core sentence from kein vs nicht Choice Gym (I have no time / I do not have time):
twist.explanation: Re-assembling "Ich habe keine Zeit" from scratch locks in the structural pattern of kein vs nicht Choice Gym without relying on short-term echo.

kein.etymology_derivation: Back-formation of nekein 'not any' (ni + ein, 'not one') — built right on ein, exactly like English none ← 'not one'. [wiktionary]

nicht.etymology_derivation: OHG niowiht: 'never a creature/thing' — the same no-thing story as English not ← nāwiht, kin to archaic wight 'being'. The gh of naught survives as German ch. [wiktionary]

können.context_translation: I can come / I am able to come.
können.etymology_derivation: Originally meant "to know/understand". Preserved in English "can", "cunning" (knowing how), "uncanny", and "beyond my ken" (beyond my knowledge).

zeit.etymology_derivation: t → z [ts] (cognate with English "tide", as in Yuletide or time and tide).

haus.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hūsą — an exact twin of English house, down to the diphthong. [wiktionary]

ente.context_phrase: Die Ente schwimmt auf dem See.
ente.context_translation: The duck swims on the lake.
ente.etymology_derivation: Middle High German ente; only Dutch eend is a cognate — no English cognate. [wiktionary]

nervös.context_phrase: Ich bin nervös vor der Prüfung.
nervös.context_translation: I am nervous before the exam.
nervös.etymology_derivation: From Latin nervōsus — the same Latin loan as English nervous. [wiktionary]

menge.context_translation: A lot of people were there.
menge.etymology_derivation: From Proto-Germanic *managį̄ — the twin of English many, which kept the older vowel. [wiktionary]

sonnenuntergang.context_phrase: Wir sehen den Sonnenuntergang am Meer.
sonnenuntergang.context_translation: We watch the sunset at the sea.
sonnenuntergang.etymology_derivation: Sonne (sun) plus Untergang (down-going: unter under, Gang a going) — three Germanic twins in a row (sun, under, gang); literally sun-under-go, while English sunset rebuilt it with set. [wiktionary]

bestimmt.etymology_derivation: The past participle of bestimmen 'to determine': determined, fixed — hence the particle sense certainly. [wiktionary]

kreditkarte.context_translation: I pay with the credit card.
kreditkarte.etymology_derivation: Kredit (credit, from Latin creditum, entrusted) + Karte (card, from Latin charta): the loan twins of English credit card. [wiktionary]

sparen.context_phrase: Ich spare Geld für den Urlaub.
sparen.context_translation: I am saving money for the vacation.
sparen.etymology_derivation: From Proto-West Germanic *sparēn; the page compares English spare — the same saving-word. [wiktionary]
